newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica cement firms weather proposed merger block.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica cement firms weather proposed merger block.

text.p: Shares in Alpha Ltd and Murray and Roberts Ltd (M&R) rose on Monday, despite an expected decision from government this week to block the proposed merger of the two cement operations.

Analysts said shares had not reacted negatively to the competition board's announcement on Friday that it would recommend the trade and industry department veto a tie-up, as a merger held no immediate benefits for shareholders.
"Benefits from the merger were rather long term than short term," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

"It had more to do with creating a favourable (capital) investment environment, rather than having a massive impact on operating margins. From a shareholder point of view a merger was indifferent," the analyst said.

He said a tie up would have started to bear fruit only in a few years time when the cement industry would need hefty capital investment for expansion, funds which companies would find difficult to muster on their own.

At 1100 GMT Alpha shares climbed 50 cents to 92.50 rand in light-volume trade of 5,400 shares. Stocks in M&R, which owns unlisted cement producer Blue Circle which would have linked up with Alpha, added 40 cents to 16.90 rand.
Johan Snyman, an analyst at brokerage Barings said shares had already discounted the likelihood of the merger being blocked.

"It was unlikely that the merger would have been accepted and this was reflected in the share price pulling back since the time of the (companies link-up) announcement," Snyman told Reuters on Monday.
The companies first announced in June that they planned to merge.
Both Alpha and M&R shares fell to their worst levels in a year late last month, with Alpha slipping to 89.75 rand and M&R shares 13.75 rand.
The competition board said on Friday it was not convinced the merger of Alpha and Blue Circle would be in the public interest.

"The Board concluded that with little prospect of new rivals entering the market as well as the negligible threat of imports, there were insufficient market pressures after the merger to ensure that these efficiencies would filter through to benefit end users of cement," it said in a statement.
